themes_detail.label: Park Noise Crisis Erupts
themes_detail.summary: Park noise complaints skyrocketed to 51 THIS WEEK, a 2,620% spike compared to the 1.9-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks, suggesting a sudden and severe noise disturbance event or pattern in Greenwich Village/SoHo parks.
evidence: 51 park noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.9 weekly average (z-score: 31.98, highest statistical anomaly in dataset)
2,620% increase represents most dramatic single spike across all complaint categories
Timing suggests event or conditions specific to current week — requires immediate field investigation
reporting_angles: What triggered the sudden spike? (Construction, event, new venue, illegal gatherings, sound systems?)
Which parks are affected? (Washington Square Park, Hudson River Park, others?)
Interview residents in adjacent buildings about sleep disruption and quality-of-life impact

themes_detail.label: Encampment Population Surge
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints surged to 60 THIS WEEK, a 380% spike from the 12.5-complaint weekly baseline, indicating a rapid increase in street homelessness or unmanaged camps across the district.
evidence: 60 encampment complaints THIS WEEK vs. 12.5 weekly average (z-score: 4.13)
Encampment remains a top-10 complaint category overall (296 complaints over 90 days)
Aligns with repeated community board budget request for public health programs — suggests chronic unaddressed issue now acute
reporting_angles: Map the locations: Are camps concentrated in specific neighborhoods (SoHo vs. Greenwich Village)?
Interview outreach workers and parks enforcement about why the spike occurred THIS WEEK specifically
Interview housed residents and business owners about visible encampments and safety concerns

themes_detail.label: Construction/Plumbing Surge
themes_detail.summary: General construction and plumbing complaints jumped 142% LAST WEEK to 23 complaints vs. the 9.5-complaint weekly average, indicating a wave of building work potentially linked to the 1,650 active DOB permits filed in the district.
evidence: 23 construction/plumbing complaints LAST WEEK vs. 9.5 weekly average (z-score: 4.44, 142% spike)
1,650 total DOB filings in 90-day period (1,440 alterations, 25 new buildings) suggests active construction wave
Elevator complaints also spiked 250% LAST WEEK (7 vs. 2.0 avg), potentially linked to construction disruptions
reporting_angles: Which DOB permit types are driving complaints? (Track 25 new buildings and 1,440 alterations)
Interview residents about noise, dust, and vibration from construction projects during peak hours
Cross-reference complaint addresses with DOB permit locations to identify problem projects

themes_detail.label: Illegal Parking Remains Elevated
themes_detail.summary: Illegal parking complaints spiked 70% LAST WEEK to 119 complaints vs. the 69.9-complaint weekly average, maintaining illegal parking as the second-highest complaint category overall (990 complaints in 90 days) with no sign of improvement.
evidence: 119 illegal parking complaints LAST WEEK vs. 69.9 weekly average (z-score: 4.42, 70% spike)
Illegal parking ranks #2 overall category with 990 complaints over 90 days
Persistent community board focus on enforcement suggests systemic under-resourcing
reporting_angles: What enforcement mechanisms exist? Are they adequately staffed given the complaint volume?
Interview parking enforcement officers about barriers to citations and compliance
Investigate whether recent permit changes or new construction have displaced parking demand

themes_detail.label: Sewer/Sidewalk Infrastructure Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Root, sewer, and sidewalk condition complaints spiked 967% three weeks ago (4 complaints vs. 0.4 weekly average), suggesting emerging infrastructure failures in the district's aging street and subsurface systems.
evidence: 4 root/sewer/sidewalk complaints 3 WEEKS AGO vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 7.49, 967% spike)
Street condition ranks #5 overall with 526 complaints in 90 days
Community board repeatedly requests catch basin cleaning and other sanitation infrastructure upgrades — suggests chronic maintenance gaps
reporting_angles: Work with DEP to identify which blocks have reported subsurface damage or tree root intrusion
Interview residents about sidewalk hazards and pedestrian safety risks
Investigate whether asbestos complaints (3 LAST WEEK, 1,100% spike) are linked to infrastructure demolition or disturbance
